newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Marketscope defends forecast Smart Car loss.
newsitem.headline: Marketscope defends forecast Smart Car loss.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Marketscope research group defended its forecast of early losses at the Smart Car joint venture between Swiss watchmaker SMH and German carmaker Mercedes-Benz AG.
Matthew Windridge, head of research at London-based Marketscope, said SMH was taking risks in projecting annual sales of 160,000 units when the car is launched in 1998 and 200,000 by the year 2000.
SMH chairman Nicolas Hayek earlier dismissed the study, which said the watchmaker's share price did not reflect the true risk of losses at Smart car maker Micro Compact Car (MCC)
Windridge said the Marketscope estimate of only 60,000 unit sales in 1998 rising to 107,000 in 2000 was based on analysis of vehicle markets and likely demand for small cars.
"This (lower sales level) would mean a signifant operating loss for MCC," he told Reuters. MCC is 49 percent held by SMH and 51 percent by Mercedes.
Windridge agreed with Hayek that it was difficult to project consumer demand for a new product like the colourful two-seater city vehicle from MCC.
But he said that was one reason he believed MCC's own sales projections were unreliable.
"We think their forecasts are risky because they are speculation," he said.
Windridge said the report's findings were based on data including market projections from world automobile forecasting group DRI.
